title: Rigveda 9.39: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.39: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.39 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 681v-682r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.39.1-2 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 29); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 681v
translation.original_text:
1ā̱śur a̍rṣa bṛhanmate̱ pari̍ pri̱yeṇa̱ dhāmnā̍ | yatra̍ de̱vā iti̱ brava̍n ||
2pa̱ri̱ṣkṛ̱ṇvann ani̍ṣkṛta̱ṁ janā̍ya yā̱taya̱nn iṣa̍ḥ | vṛ̱ṣṭiṁ di̱vaḥ pari̍ srava ||
translation.text:
1FLOW On, O thou of lofty thought, flow swift in thy beloved form, Saying, I go where dwell the Gods.
2Preparing what is unprepared, and bringing store of food to man, Make thou the rain descend from heaven.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 681v (numbered 103v by the scribe) (OPenn image 682, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.37.5 ‹-asarat›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 682r (numbered 104r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.39.3 ‹vi-rocayan›. Verses 9.39.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1āśuḥ | arṣa | bṛhat-mate | pari | priyeṇa | dhāmnā | yatra | devāḥ | iti | bravan
2pari-kṛṇvan | aniḥ-kṛtam | janāya | yātayan | iṣaḥ | vṛṣṭim | divaḥ | pari | srava

translation.original_ref: RV 9.39.3-6 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 29); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 682r
translation.original_text:
3su̱ta e̍ti pa̱vitra̱ ā tviṣi̱ṁ dadhā̍na̱ oja̍sā | vi̱cakṣā̍ṇo viro̱caya̍n ||
4a̱yaṁ sa yo di̱vas pari̍ raghu̱yāmā̍ pa̱vitra̱ ā | sindho̍r ū̱rmā vy akṣa̍rat ||
5ā̱vivā̍san parā̱vato̱ atho̍ arvā̱vata̍ḥ su̱taḥ | indrā̍ya sicyate̱ madhu̍ ||
6sa̱mī̱cī̱nā a̍nūṣata̱ hari̍ṁ hinva̱nty adri̍bhiḥ | yonā̍v ṛ̱tasya̍ sīdata ||
translation.text:
3With might, bestowing power, thejuice enters the purifying sieve, Far-seeing, sending forth its light.
4This is it which in rapid course hath with the river's wave flowed down From heaven upon the straining cloth.
5Inviting him from far away, and even from near at hand, the juice For Indra is poured forth as meath.
6In union they have sung the hymn: with stones they urge the Tawny One. Sit in the place of sacrifice.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 682r (numbered 104r by the scribe) (OPenn image 682, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.39.3 ‹vi-rocayan›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 682v (numbered 104v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.41.1 ‹ayāsaḥ akramuḥ ghnantaḥ kṛṣṇām›. Verses 9.39.3-6 end on this page; 9.39.3 begins on fol. 681v (numbered 103v by the scribe).

3sutaḥ | eti | pavitre | ā | tviṣim | dadhānaḥ | ojasā | vi-cakṣāṇaḥ | vi-rocayan
4ayam | saḥ | yaḥ | divaḥ | pari | raghu-yāmā | pavitre | ā | sindhoḥ | ūrmā | vi | akṣarat
5āvivāsan | parāvataḥ | atho iti | arvāvataḥ | sutaḥ | indrāya | sicyate | madhu
6samīcīnāḥ | anūṣata | harim | hinvanti | adri-bhiḥ | yonau | ṛtasya | sīdata
